channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee touches an eight-month high near 92.2, erasing its losses for the financial year
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · The rupee opened at 92.65 per dollar on Wednesday and rose to 92.29 during the day, up 56 paise from Monday's close, PTI reported in the afternoon. PTI says that wipes out all the rupee's losses since the financial year began in April, and calls it an eight-month high. DSIJ puts the day's best level at 92.18 and InCred Money reports 92.21, its strongest since 12 March. Currency markets were shut on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti. Analysts quoted by PTI credit large inflows from foreign investors into Indian shares and Brent crude slipping below $90 a barrel. Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,672.99 crore of Indian shares on Monday, per exchange data cited by PTI. A stronger rupee makes imports such as fuel and foreign travel slightly cheaper.

item.title: India markets: Nifty climbs 1.85% to 25,819 as consumer and bank shares recover
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Trading resumed after Tuesday's Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. The Nifty opened about 309 points higher at 25,658, according to Liquide, and closed up 469.60 points (1.85%) at 25,819.25, according to Kotak Neo, Liquide and DSIJ. That recovers most of Monday's fall. The Sensex rose 1,502.29 points (1.82%) to 83,938.28. The reports credit continued buying by foreign investors, lower crude oil prices and a stronger rupee. Consumer goods (FMCG) shares led: the Nifty FMCG index rose 3.79% and pharma 2.38%. Nifty Bank rose 1.79% to 63,703.25, per Liquide. Metal shares fell again (Nifty Metal −2.04%), which DSIJ links to Tata Steel's proposed deal with APL Apollo Tubes. Hindustan Unilever (+6.08%) gained the most in the Nifty and Tata Steel (−2.27%) fell the most, per Liquide and DSIJ. Smaller companies lagged: the Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 0.44%, per Kotak Neo.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Kremlin says it does not yet see what Europe would add to the talks; no date for the next round
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Europeans are insisting on a four-party format for the talks, but "we do not yet fully understand what added value European participation can bring", per UNITED24 citing Russian state media. TASS quotes him as saying "the date has not yet been set" for the next round. US envoy Jared Kushner had said Russia accepted talks that include Europe. Separately, Zelenskyy told Bloomberg he will ask the new US Congress, which meets in January, for more military aid and tougher sanctions on Russia if no peace deal is reached, per a report on the interview by Antiwar.com.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Putin vows retaliation for Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries; Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills two
item.description: 23–24 Nov 2026 · At a Kremlin meeting with oil executives on 24 November, President Putin said "the Kyiv regime continues to attack our refining facilities, despite the U.S. president's appeal", and that "retaliatory measures on our part are inevitable", per Reuters and The Moscow Times. The night before, a Russian strike on the city of Zaporizhzhia partly destroyed a five-storey apartment block, killing two people, said Mykhailo Semikin, head of the regional military administration. Children were among the injured.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Russian drone briefly enters Polish airspace; Poland says a NATO jet was cleared to fire on the 20 November missile
item.description: 23–24 Nov 2026 · Late on 23 November a Russian drone "briefly violated Polish airspace" during attacks on western Ukraine, Poland's military said. Permission to shoot it down was given, but it was not fired on after it turned east, because of the risk to people on the ground, per ABC News. It flew over Dorohusk, a border town with a major rail and freight crossing, for several minutes. A deputy defence minister said Poland assumes it was deliberate; Russia's ambassador said no convincing evidence has been shown. Separately, Poland's operational commander, Lt Gen Ireneusz Nowak, said a Swedish Gripen jet under NATO command was cleared to fire at a Russian cruise missile on 20 November, but bad weather stopped the pilot finding it, per Fox News. Poland has again asked the US for permanent troops. Estonia's foreign minister wrote that closing the border "will limit opportunities for hostile intelligence activities", per TIME.

item.title: US ground stop: Duffy and FAA chief to face Congress over the ground stop
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy will testify next week before a Senate subcommittee about the 13 November ground stop (14 November in India), Reuters reports. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford goes before a House panel on 1 December. On 2 December a Senate Commerce aviation subcommittee will question Duffy about his request for $50 billion to modernise air traffic control and airports. Reuters says the outage led to more than 18,000 cancelled flights and disrupted travel for 1.5 million people. Some Republicans think Congress may approve as little as $10 billion. Senator Jerry Moran said the $50 billion figure "appeared to come out of the blue". The hearings come in Thanksgiving week, which the FAA expects to be its busiest in years.

item.title: Delhi air: Tuesday's daily AQI 227, 'poor'; forecast says 'poor' until 27 November
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Delhi's 24-hour average AQI was 227 ('poor') on Tuesday, down from 260 on Monday, PTI reports from CPCB data. Of 58 stations, 34 were 'poor', 19 'moderate' and 5 'very poor'. Delhi Cantonment was worst at 346. The morning was worse: Business Standard put the city at 242 at 7 am, with 10 of 57 stations 'very poor'. Stage II curbs stay in force. The government's early-warning system expects 'poor' air from 24 to 27 November, then 'poor' to 'very poor' for six days. Satellites spotted 404 farm fires across seven states on Monday, most in Uttar Pradesh (174) and Madhya Pradesh (154).

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Nvidia shares fall about 6%, giving back part of Monday's jump
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia shares closed down 5.86% on Tuesday, a day after rising about 31% on Huang's return. Chip shares fell widely: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 7.88%. Reports pointed to profit-taking and to the investigations that are still open, including the criminal inquiry into Megaspeed and the board's own review of Huang, which it did not finish before reinstating him. Morningstar's Lindsey Stewart said the return "is going to add to those corporate governance questions that investors have". Senator Elizabeth Warren said Nvidia's board and executives still owe Congress answers on export controls.

item.title: AI this week: AI shares fall back; Anthropic closes below its IPO price and the US blacklists Megaspeed
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic shares fell about 6.5% to about $81.90, the first close below the $83 IPO price. Nvidia fell 5.86% after Monday's 31% jump, and the Philadelphia chip index lost 7.88%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48%. The day before, the US Commerce Department put Megaspeed, the Singapore firm at the centre of the Nvidia reports, and six other companies, including an Alibaba unit, on its trade blacklist; Alibaba called the listing of its unit "erroneous".

item.title: OpenAI: Former engineer accused of bugging an OpenAI meeting room is freed on bail
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · A federal magistrate judge released a former OpenAI engineer on a $1 million bond before a trial set for January, The Wall Street Journal reported, per Fox Business. He was arrested by the FBI in October and has pleaded not guilty to a charge of illegally recording conversations. Prosecutors allege he hid a recording device in an executive conference room in September. New filings say investigators found hundreds of audio files on his computer, including dozens of recordings of OpenAI meetings that may involve trade secrets and legal advice. His lawyer says he was a curious "tinkerer" and that the government's spying claims have collapsed. He has not been charged with espionage. OpenAI said in October it had no sign that its model weights were accessed.

item.title: Anthropic: Shares close below the $83 IPO price for the first time
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic shares fell about 6.5% on Tuesday, its fourth day of trading, to close at about $81.90, below the $83 IPO price. They touched $75.61 during the day. AI and chip shares fell broadly as Nvidia gave back part of Monday's rally. A filing showed CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei each sold 3,378,378 shares, worth about $280 million, at the IPO price; this was a planned sale to the underwriters as part of the offering, not a sale on the market. Analysts at Canaccord Genuity, Wedbush and Oppenheimer started covering the shares with buy-type ratings.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Brent rebounds 2.3% to $91.40 on new tanker attacks
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Brent crude for January rose 2.3% to settle at $91.40 a barrel on Tuesday, after early losses, per Bloomberg (via Rigzone) and Seeking Alpha. US crude (WTI) rose 2.4% to $82.05. Reports of more attacks on ships near Hormuz, and Iran's vow to tighten control of the strait, outweighed signs of a supply surplus. The IEA says Gulf crude exports are back to 74% of pre-war levels, per Bloomberg. Trading was thin before the US Thanksgiving holiday, which can exaggerate moves.

item.title: US midterms: AP calls Tennessee's 4th district for Democrat Victoria Broderick
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · The Associated Press called Tennessee's 4th House district for Democrat Victoria Broderick over Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais at 11:12 am Central time on 24 November, per NewsChannel 9. She led by 361 votes when the race was called, Roll Call reports, three weeks after election day. DesJarlais had already said his campaign finished "just a few hundred votes short". Roll Call says three House races are still not called, including two Louisiana seats going to December runoffs and Minnesota's 1st district, which is heading for a hand recount.

item.title: US trade deal: Report: US may raise tariffs on India and others as soon as this week
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · The US may announce new tariffs on China, India and other countries as early as this week, the Wall Street Journal reported, according to PTI and IBTimes. They would follow a probe the US Trade Representative opened in March into 16 economies. It looks at whether government subsidies helped firms make far more than they can sell, flooding world markets with cheap goods. IBTimes, citing the Journal, says India and Vietnam could face higher duties, while Japan, South Korea and the EU could stay at 15% or less under their trade deals. No rates have been set, and the timing could change. It is one of the pending 'Section 301' probes that India's Commerce Secretary said must be settled before the deal can be signed. No Indian government response was reported. For exporters, a higher US duty would make Indian goods dearer in their biggest market.

item.title: Russian oil: India on course for record Russian oil imports in 2026, but refiners expect less next year
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · India imported an average of 1.99 million barrels a day of Russian crude this year up to early November, about 250,000 more than a year earlier, according to Kpler data cited by Reuters. Trade sources told Reuters that Russian oil made up about 38% of India's imports from January to October. Refiners expect a full-year average of about 1.9 million barrels a day. India and China together are buying more than 80% of Russia's crude exports, two industry sources said. Indian refiners told Reuters their purchases are likely to fall back to pre-Iran-war levels in 2027 if Gulf supplies return to normal, with price deciding how much they buy.

item.title: US markets: Nasdaq falls 1.5% as the Nvidia rally fades; Dow rises 0.9% and closes above 50,000
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq 1.48% to 23,733.54, per AP (via La Nación) and BigGo Finance. The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70. Chip and AI shares gave back part of Monday's rally. Nvidia fell 5.86% to $155.38, per Reuters data via MarketScreener, and the Philadelphia chip index fell 7.88%, per BigGo Finance. One analyst told Reuters that "one headline doesn't really resolve investor questions about the AI trade." Reports that the US may soon raise tariffs on China and other trading partners also weighed on shares, per TipRanks and Reuters. Retailers rose after strong results: Dollar Tree gained about 11%. A Conference Board survey showed consumer confidence rose to 103.3 in November, above the 92.5 economists expected, which helped the Dow. Anthropic shares fell below their $83 IPO price; TipRanks puts the day's fall at 8%. Traders expect the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points in December, per the CME FedWatch tool. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure; at 10:05 am the S&P 500 was down 0.5% after falling as much as 1.4%, per AP.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: Congress leaves for Thanksgiving with no deal; White House sends its list for the next stopgap
item.description: 20–23 Nov 2026 · Congress left for the Thanksgiving break without a funding deal. Of the 12 yearly spending bills, the House has passed three and the Senate none, per The Center Square, and appropriators in both parties expect another short-term stopgap. On 23 November the White House sent Congress its list of 'anomalies', exceptions to a stopgap's freeze on spending, per SpacePolicyOnline. It asks for $5 billion for the Golden Dome missile-defence programme and $2 billion for NASA's Artemis Moon programme, among other items, per SpacePolicyOnline and Breaking Defense. Punchbowl reports the new stopgap would notionally run to 31 March, but the White House list gives no end date, SpacePolicyOnline says. A funding law needs 60 Senate votes, so at least seven Democrats must back it.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: US puts Megaspeed and six other companies on its trade blacklist
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 (US time) · The US Commerce Department added Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company at the centre of the reports about Huang, to its Entity List with six other companies in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand. They include Apex Enterprise Solutions, a Singapore unit of Alibaba. US firms now need a licence to sell them American goods, software or technology, including chips, and applications are normally refused. Commerce says the companies pose a "significant risk" of passing advanced computing items to unauthorised users. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. Alibaba called the listing of its unit "erroneous" and said it will seek legal remedies. Nvidia says it stopped selling to Megaspeed in June 2025. US prosecutors are running a criminal investigation into Megaspeed.

item.title: AI this week: Anthropic posts a second Claude-made proof, of a 1979 conjecture; Meta's AI chief says 'superintelligence is arriving'
item.description: 22–23 Nov 2026 · Anthropic published a 70-page paper credited to Claude that claims to prove Valiant's 1979 "VP ≠ VNP" conjecture about how hard some formulas are to compute. A computer check passed, but no human mathematician has verified it, and it does not solve P vs NP. A day earlier Meta's chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, wrote that "superintelligence is arriving" and called for urgent safety work. China's Zhipu released GLM-5.4, a flagship model that runs its layers twice. The New York Times reported that Elon Musk told SpaceX staff in August to "sell compute because we can't compete"; Anthropic and Google rent its AI computers.

item.title: AI model tracker: Zhipu: GLM-5.4
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Zhipu's new flagship runs its layers twice (a "loop" design). Zhipu says it matches 2–3 trillion-parameter models from a 750-billion-parameter base, with image input; no benchmark scores yet. In its coding plan and chat app; API and open weights later.

item.title: Anthropic: Anthropic posts a Claude-written proof of a 1979 maths conjecture; no human has checked it yet
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Anthropic published a 70-page paper, "VP ≠ VNP over every field", credited to Claude, with a computer-checkable version in the Lean language, in its public formal-math repository. It claims to settle Valiant's 1979 conjecture: that some maths formulas (such as the "permanent" of a grid of numbers) cannot be worked out with small arithmetic circuits, unlike the related "determinant". Anthropic says an internal research model found the result. The computer check passed, but the repository warns that no machine checks whether the formal statement says what is claimed, and Anthropic says no human mathematician has verified it. The paper says it does not solve the better-known P vs NP problem. Complexity researcher Lance Fortnow called it "likely correct" after a first look, not a full check.

item.title: xAI & Grok: NYT: Musk told staff to 'sell compute because we can't compete'
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The New York Times reports that in August Elon Musk renamed a SpaceX AI group chat of hundreds of engineers "Sell compute because we can't compete", and warned that anyone "wasting GPUs" while the company was "failing to compete" would be asked to leave. Musk told staff that renting out its Colossus computers to rivals had become more lucrative than using them for SpaceX's own AI products, per the Times. It reports that Anthropic is now SpaceX's biggest customer, Google is also a client, and the AI unit accounts for more than half of SpaceX's revenue. SpaceX did not comment, per Forbes.

item.title: China's AI labs: Zhipu releases GLM-5.4, built by running its layers twice
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Zhipu (Z.ai) released GLM-5.4, its new flagship. Instead of adding layers, it runs 28 layers of its GLM-5 base model twice, a "loop" design meant to improve reasoning without more parameters. Zhipu says it matches models of 2 to 3 trillion parameters, from a 750-billion-parameter base; it has not yet published benchmark scores. It adds image understanding and, per TechNode, a one-million-token context window. It is available in Zhipu's coding plan and chat app. The API and open weights will follow safety checks, with no date.

item.title: China's AI labs: US blacklists an Alibaba unit and Megaspeed over chip diversion
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 (US time) · The US Commerce Department put seven companies on its Entity List, including Megaspeed of Singapore and Apex Enterprise Solutions, Alibaba's Singapore unit. US firms now need a licence, normally refused, to sell them chips and other technology. Commerce says they pose a "significant risk" of passing advanced computing items to unauthorised users. Alibaba called the listing "erroneous", said the unit "has never diverted" restricted chips and plans legal action. Beijing called US claims of a Chinese intelligence operation "groundless speculation".

item.title: West Asia & oil: Brent falls to a three-month low as Gulf exports hold up
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Brent crude for January delivery settled at $89.37 a barrel on Monday, down about 3.5% from $92.57 on Friday and its lowest in about three months, per FinanceFeeds and Kotak Neo. Analysts said signs that Gulf crude exports are holding up outweighed weekend attacks on shipping and on Bahrain, per Investing.com and Tradingpedia. Libya's Sharara pipeline also reopened. The International Energy Agency expects supply to exceed demand by about 2 million barrels a day in October–December. Analysts at IG said a new US strike on Iran looks less likely for now. Lower oil prices help India, which imports most of its crude.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Three tankers hit near Hormuz; Iran's army chief says the strait must be 'closed further'
item.description: 22–23 Nov 2026 · Three Liberian-flagged supertankers owned by South Korea's Sinokor were hit within about 20 minutes on the evening of 22 November (UTC) as they left the eastern end of the Strait of Hormuz, per a revised UKMTO report cited by Maritime Executive. All crew were accounted for and the ships carried on. It is not clear whether these are the ships Iran says hit mines. On 23 November Iran's army commander, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, said Hormuz "must be closed further day by day" until Iran's seven conditions are met, per Euronews. Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said there would be "no negotiation" before then. The same day Qatar's prime minister met US Vice-President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington to try to restart US–Iran talks, per AP.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee ends its rally, closing 30 paise weaker at 92.92 as Indian shares fall
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The rupee settled 30 paise weaker at 92.92 per dollar on Monday (provisional), PTI reports via Telangana Today. It had strengthened to 92.43 early on, helped by cheaper oil, but weakened as Indian shares fell sharply; it touched 93.11 during the day. A dealer at Mirae Asset Sharekhan linked the fall to the drop in Indian shares. A firm US dollar, near a 19-month high, also weighed, per Angel One. Brent crude was at $92.08 a barrel, down 0.53%. Angel One describes the move as the rupee easing slightly from a seven-month high.

item.title: Ebola: WHO says fighting in Ituri trapped health workers; its chief says "the best medicine is peace"
item.description: 22–23 Nov 2026 · WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said fighting near a hospital in Ituri forced health workers to shelter in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours, putting the response at "grave risk". "The best medicine is peace," he said. WHO has verified more than 87 attacks on health care in Congo this year. The UN's Ebola coordinator said fighters of the ADF armed group had recently killed more people than Ebola had.

item.title: Meta AI: Meta's AI chief says 'superintelligence is arriving'
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, wrote on X that "superintelligence is arriving", pointing to the Claude-assisted Riemann proof. He said he doubts people could control AI that keeps improving itself, called for urgent work on safety, alignment and security, and said "how humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence". He urged the industry to change course. The tone differs from Mark Zuckerberg, who has rejected calls for a coordinated slowdown, Al Jazeera notes. Meta has not announced any change in policy.

item.title: Ebola: Outbreak passes 11,600 confirmed cases and 5,600 deaths across eight Congo provinces
item.description: 15–17 Nov 2026 · As of 17 November the US CDC counted 11,645 confirmed cases and 5,683 deaths, of which 11,613 cases and 5,678 deaths were in Congo. Europe's disease agency ECDC, citing Congo's health institute, said the outbreak covers 68 of 178 health zones in 8 provinces. UNICEF says children are 28% of cases and 35% of deaths. Cases have also been confirmed in Uganda (where the outbreak was declared over), Kenya, Nigeria and France. Suspected cases in Congo are temporarily left out of the count while data are standardised, so totals may change. AP reported that Africa CDC has raised concerns about more than $700 million in Ebola aid it cannot account for.

item.title: Ebola: US makes every air passenger sign that they have not been in Congo
item.description: 3 Nov 2026 · A US CDC order took effect at 11:59 pm Eastern time. Every passenger flying to the US, from any country, must sign a statement that they have not been in the DRC in the previous 21 days. Airlines must refuse boarding to anyone who does not sign. The order runs to 18 December unless it is changed.

item.title: Ebola: Nigeria confirms a case in Abuja, the first in West Africa
item.description: 20 Oct 2026 · Nigeria's health ministry confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja in a woman who had arrived from Uganda. It was the outbreak's first spread to West Africa. Officials were tracing 44 contacts. AP put the outbreak at more than 9,000 infections and more than 4,300 deaths.

item.title: Ebola: Kenya confirms its first case after a patient from Congo dies in Nairobi
item.description: 6 Oct 2026 · Kenya's health ministry confirmed the country's first Ebola case. The patient, a Kenyan man who had lived in Congo, travelled by road to Uganda and flew to Nairobi on 3 October, where he died. Officials identified 28 contacts. Congo had passed 8,300 confirmed cases and 4,000 deaths, per Al Jazeera.

item.title: Ebola: Congo starts vaccinating health workers with a vaccine made for a different Ebola strain
item.description: 27 Aug 2026 · Congo began vaccinating health workers in Kisangani with Ervebo, a vaccine approved only for the Zaire strain of Ebola, not Bundibugyo. It is being given under compassionate use, meaning it is untested against this strain. WHO approved 70,000 doses: about 50,000 for front-line workers and about 20,000 for a trial. The government count at the time was 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 deaths.

item.title: Ebola: India screens arrivals and advises against non-essential travel to Congo, Uganda and South Sudan
item.description: 21–23 May 2026 · India's health services directorate issued an advisory, displayed at Delhi airport, for passengers arriving from the DRC, Uganda and South Sudan. They must report any symptoms before immigration, and anyone who falls ill within 21 days of arriving should seek care. On 23 May the Union health ministry advised Indians to avoid non-essential travel to the three countries.

item.title: Ebola: WHO declares the Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda a global health emergency
item.description: 17 May 2026 · The World Health Organization declared an outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern, its highest alarm. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. WHO said it was not a pandemic emergency and advised countries not to close borders. As of 16 May there were 8 laboratory-confirmed cases, 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths in Congo's Ituri province, and 2 confirmed cases in Uganda among travellers from Congo, one of whom died.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Zelenskyy warns Russia is preparing new strikes; five hurt in an attack on central Kyiv
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · In his nightly address, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia preparing new strikes, and asked the US and other partners to take note because their decisions affect air-defence supplies, per Reuters. A Russian attack on central Kyiv on Monday injured five people. French President Macron said "we must reopen the question of Ukraine's membership to NATO". No date has been set for the next round of talks, and the agreed prisoner exchange has not been reported as carried out.

item.title: Russia and NATO: NATO sends a radar plane to Poland; Russia warns Estonia of 'open war'
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · NATO ambassadors met in Brussels, and NATO's top military commander ordered an AWACS early-warning radar plane to Poland. NATO said Russia "bears full responsibility" for the missiles. Poland did not formally ask for Article 4 talks this time. The same day Russia's foreign ministry summoned Estonia's acting envoy in Moscow and said Estonia was "on the verge of triggering open war". Estonia denied letting Ukraine use its airspace.

item.title: Budget 2027: Finance Minister holds 10 rounds of pre-Budget talks
item.description: 17–23 Nov 2026 · Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has now held 10 pre-Budget meetings. Since 17 November she met groups from manufacturing; small businesses and startups; capital markets, banking and insurance; IT; infrastructure, energy and sustainability; jobs and labour; housing, cities and culture; and, on 23 November, health and social sectors. The ministry has not said what was suggested. The Budget is expected on 1 February 2027.

item.title: Delhi air: Monday morning AQI 236, 'poor'; air commission sets a 15–20% pollution-cut target for 2027
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI was 236 ('poor') at 8 am on Monday, per CPCB data reported by IANS. Some stations were 'very poor', including Sirifort (333), Talkatora (317) and ITO (301). Stage II curbs stay in force. The Commission for Air Quality Management told Delhi and nearby states to write 2027 action plans that cut overall pollution by at least 15%, aiming for 20%. For the first time the plans must include district-level plans and name the officers responsible. Forecasts expect 'poor' air until Wednesday, then 'poor' to 'very poor'.
